text: Designing a good REST API is like creating a clear map for other developers. First, you should use simple, logical endpoints that represent resources, such as `/users` or `/orders`. Always return proper HTTP status codes—like `200` for success, `404` when something is not found, and `500` for server errors—so clients know exactly what happened. Versioning is also crucial; adding `/v1/` to your URL prevents breaking changes for existing users. Finally, never skip documentation. Clear examples of requests and responses help others adopt your API quickly, reducing confusion and support questions. Good design saves time for everyone.
